subject.title: [Bug] Command validation bypass on multi-line tool calls in parser

question: Is there enough sanitized evidence to classify this as a confirmed command-execution security vulnerability, or should triage wait for a concrete payload and execution trace?
rationale: The report alleges a security-boundary bypass, but current source and dependency contracts contain multiple later validation layers and no supplied evidence identifies which one fails.

options.title: Request a sanitized reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open and require the exact tool-call payload, schema, version/provider, logs, and resulting command-policy decision before assigning a fix.

options.title: Route privately after confirmation
options.body: If maintainers can independently reproduce unauthorized execution, move detailed exploit handling to the repository's private security-advisory process.

recommendation.title: Request a sanitized reproduction
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require the exact tool-call payload, schema, version/provider, logs, and resulting command-policy decision before assigning a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the closest related tool-call repair boundary and can route the security proof decision to the appropriate owner.
